title: CybICS CTF Training
description: Industrial Control Systems Security Training Platform

basic_understanding.name: Basic Understanding
basic_understanding.description: Fundamental understanding of industrial processes and control systems

challenges.title: Understanding the Physical Process
challenges.description: Learn about industrial processes and control systems
challenges.hint: Log in to the FUXA HMI as operator, switch the plant to manual and give the gas nowhere to go. Click Verify while the HMI shows BLOW-OUT.

challenges.title: PLC Programming
challenges.description: Introduction to PLC programming and control logic
challenges.hint: Modify the CybICS program in OpenPLC Editor, compile it, then upload and start it via the web UI on port 8080. Then click Verify.

network_analysis.name: Network Analysis
network_analysis.description: Network reconnaissance and traffic analysis techniques

challenges.title: Service Scanning
challenges.description: Discover network services and open ports
challenges.hint: Use network scanning tools to discover open ports and services

challenges.title: S7comm Scanning
challenges.description: Analyze Siemens S7 communication
challenges.hint: Focus on Siemens S7 protocol communication patterns

challenges.title: HMI Project Recon
challenges.description: The HMI knows every register of the plant and which button writes which one. Get its project without logging in, map the plant from it and enter what you found.
challenges.hint: An HMI page in a browser has to get its screens from somewhere. Watch the requests it makes while it loads, then repeat the big one yourself without a token.

answers.name: plc
answers.label: PLC endpoint the HMI polls (host:port)

answers.name: stop_register
answers.label: Holding register the STOP / SHUTDOWN button writes (wire address, from 0)

answers.name: compressor_coil
answers.label: Coil the SystemView "Comp." button toggles (wire address, from 0)

answers.name: hpt_tag_id
answers.label: FUXA tag ID of the HPT tag

challenges.title: Packet Anatomy
challenges.description: No library, no Wireshark: build Modbus/TCP frames byte by byte, send the read-only ones to the PLC over a raw TCP connection and take its answers apart. Hand in four frames as hex.
challenges.hint: Every frame is a 7-byte MBAP header plus the PDU. The length field counts only what follows it, and a read or write always covers one contiguous block of registers.

answers.name: read_request
answers.label: Read request: GST and HPT in one frame, no more than needed (hex)

answers.name: read_response
answers.label: The PLC's response to exactly that request (hex)

answers.name: write_request
answers.label: Write request: STOP and MANUAL to 0 in one frame, not sent (hex)

answers.name: exception
answers.label: The PLC's answer to a read of a holding register it does not have (hex)

challenges.title: Wireshark Capture
challenges.description: Learn network traffic analysis
challenges.hint: Look for unusual protocols or data patterns in network traffic

security_testing.name: Security Testing
security_testing.description: Test system resilience and security mechanisms

challenges.title: Flood & Overwrite
challenges.description: Test system resilience against flooding attacks
challenges.hint: Flood the HPT setpoint register with Modbus writes, then click Verify.

challenges.title: Plant Physics Sandbox
challenges.description: Know what the plant will do before you touch it. Use the plant sandbox in the Theory Path to predict three situations an attacker can create: the outputs frozen with and without the refill, and one forged pressure reading. Then name the register that takes the PLC out of the game with a single write.
challenges.hint: The sandbox counts the ticks in which the compressor really moved gas, and its log says why it stopped. The plant's guard on the GST and the PLC's guard are not the same.

answers.name: settle_hpt
answers.label: Situation 1: HPT at which the plant comes to rest (bar)

answers.name: blowout_tick
answers.label: Situation 2: tick on which the blow-out valve opens

answers.name: spoof_ticks
answers.label: Situation 3: ticks the compressor moves gas before the PLC stops it

answers.name: freeze_register
answers.label: Holding register an attacker writes once to freeze the outputs

challenges.title: FUXA Password Attack
challenges.description: Brute-force the FUXA HMI login and enter the administrator credentials you recovered
challenges.hint: FUXA logs in with JSON at /api/signin. Run ffuf with a JSON body and filter out the answers that contain an error, then enter the user name and password that worked.

answers.name: username
answers.label: FUXA user name

answers.name: password
answers.label: Password

challenges.title: OpenPLC Password Attack
challenges.description: Brute-force the OpenPLC web login and recover the flag from the user account
challenges.hint: Brute-force the OpenPLC admin login at port 8080 with ffuf, then read the flag from the user account details on the Users page.

challenges.title: OPC-UA
challenges.description: Explore OPC-UA protocol security
challenges.hint: Check for default credentials or weak authentication

challenges.title: Fuzzing Modbus
challenges.description: Test Modbus protocol robustness
challenges.hint: Fuzz the Modbus server including diagnostic function codes, then click Verify.

challenges.title: S7 Side Door
challenges.description: The Modbus port can be firewalled, but the PLC also speaks S7comm. Stop the plant through OpenPLC's S7 server on port 102.
challenges.hint: OpenPLC's Snap7 server maps the %MW memory words to data block DB1002, two bytes per word. Write 1 to the stop flag over S7comm, click Verify while the plant is stopped, then write 0 back.

challenges.title: Forged HMI Token
challenges.description: FUXA trusts any session token signed with its key, and the default key is in its public source code. Forge an administrator token for a user that does not exist and paste it here.
challenges.hint: FUXA is open source. When nobody sets a signing key in its settings, which key does it fall back to, and where in its code is that written down?

answers.name: token
answers.label: Forged FUXA token (JWT)

challenges.title: The Forgotten API
challenges.description: The PLC's web login is not its only management interface. Find OpenPLC's second API, claim it with an account of your own and enter that account's credentials here.
challenges.hint: The PLC has more than one web server. Scan beyond the well-known ports, and when you find one that speaks HTTPS, ask it how many users it has.

answers.name: username
answers.label: User name of your API account

answers.name: password
answers.label: Its password (at least 8 characters, a throwaway one)

challenges.title: DNP3 Side Door
challenges.description: OpenPLC also runs a DNP3 outstation that nothing in the plant uses. Find it, learn its link addresses, and stop the plant with a DNP3 frame you build yourself.
challenges.hint: A DNP3 station only answers frames addressed to its own link address and coming from the master it is configured for. Link-layer requests are cheap: ask every pair in a small range and see which one answers. The README explains the frame format and the CRC.

challenges.title: Stop Means Stop?
challenges.description: Send the PLC an S7comm CPU STOP. It will acknowledge it and swear it has stopped. Prove from the plant whether that is true, then start the CPU again.
challenges.hint: Do not trust a status your client library reports without asking the PLC: read the CPU's status list (SZL 0x0424) yourself. Verify while the PLC says STOP, then warm-restart it.

challenges.title: Man-in-the-Middle (MitM)
challenges.description: Learn about network interception
challenges.hint: Run the arpspoof man-in-the-middle between FUXA and the PLC, then click Verify.

challenges.title: UART Training Guide
challenges.description: Hardware-level communication (requires hardware)
challenges.hint: Monitor serial communications for credentials or commands

challenges.title: Detect Port Scan
challenges.description: Perform a port scan and verify the IDS detected it — find the flag in the IDS rule stats
challenges.hint: Run a port scan, then query the IDS at /api/rules/stats — the flag appears when the port_scan rule has fired

challenges.title: Detect Modbus Flooding
challenges.description: Launch a Modbus flooding attack, analyze it with the IDS, and find the flag in the rule stats
challenges.hint: Run the override script, then query /api/rules/stats — the flag appears when the modbus_flood rule fires

ids_challenges.name: IDS Challenges
ids_challenges.description: Interact with the Intrusion Detection System — trigger alerts, analyze incidents, and evade detection

challenges.title: IDS Challenge
challenges.description: Trigger the intrusion detection system by performing attacks and retrieve the flag
challenges.hint: Perform multiple different attacks and check the IDS flag endpoint

challenges.title: IDS Forensics
challenges.description: Analyze IDS alert data to investigate a security incident
challenges.hint: Use the /api/summary and /api/alerts endpoints to gather data about the incident

challenges.title: Incident PCAP
challenges.description: Someone stopped the plant three times in one night. A capture from the PLC's mirror port is all you have. Find the device behind it, even where it wore other hosts' addresses, and rebuild the timeline.
challenges.hint: An IP address is just a claim. Look one layer lower: which Ethernet address sent the frames that claim to come from the HMI, and did that change during the night?

answers.name: attacker_mac
answers.label: MAC address of the rogue device

answers.name: attacker_ips
answers.label: Every IP address the rogue device used or impersonated (comma separated)

answers.name: poison_frame
answers.label: Frame number of the first frame in which the rogue device claims another host's IP address

answers.name: stop_frames
answers.label: Frame numbers of the three requests that stopped the plant (comma separated)

challenges.title: Physics Never Lies
challenges.description: One night the compressor ran for minutes on end while the HMI showed a calm, normal tank. The historian export is all you have. Use the plant's physics to find the forged value, the moment it started to lie and the real pressure it was hiding.
challenges.hint: Write down what the plant can do in one cycle: how much gas the compressor takes from the GST and how much it puts into the HPT. Then find the first row that breaks that rule, not the first row that looks odd.

answers.name: forged_value
answers.label: Which recorded value was forged? (column name or register)

answers.name: first_forged
answers.label: Time stamp of the first row the plant cannot have produced

answers.name: true_hpt
answers.label: Real HPT pressure in the last row of the export, in bar

challenges.title: IDS Evasion
challenges.description: Perform a stealth Modbus write without triggering any IDS alerts
challenges.hint: Study the IDS detection thresholds on the Rules tab and send writes slowly

challenges.title: Trusted Writer
challenges.description: The IDS never counts Modbus writes from the HMI. Stop the plant so that the command reaches the PLC from FUXA, not from your host: make the HMI send it for you, raise no IDS alert, keep the plant stopped and click Verify.
challenges.hint: FUXA writes a tag for whoever asks it the right way. HMI Project Recon tells you the stop tag's ID; the HMI page in your browser shows you how it asks.

defense.name: Defense & Hardening
defense.description: Harden the ICS environment by applying defensive security measures

challenges.title: Harden OpenPLC Credentials
challenges.description: Change the default OpenPLC password to prevent unauthorized access
challenges.hint: Log into the OpenPLC web UI at port 8080 and change the default password from 'openplc'

challenges.title: Harden FUXA Credentials
challenges.description: Change the default FUXA admin password to prevent unauthorized HMI access
challenges.hint: Access FUXA at port 1881 and change the admin password from its default value

challenges.title: Rotate the FUXA Token Key
challenges.description: Give FUXA a signing key of its own so tokens forged with the published default key are refused
challenges.hint: The key lives in /_appdata/settings.js inside the FUXA container (admin shell, docker exec). Put it on its own line straight after 'module.exports = {' rather than uncommenting the example further down, check the file still loads with node, then restart FUXA.

challenges.title: Modbus Firewall Rules
challenges.description: Restrict Modbus (port 502) access so only authorized systems can communicate with the PLC
challenges.hint: Use iptables on the OpenPLC container to only allow 172.18.0.4 (FUXA) to access port 502

challenges.title: Close the Side Doors
challenges.description: The PLC speaks six protocols and the plant needs two. Find out which ones are really used, switch off S7, DNP3 and EtherNet/IP, block the REST API that has no switch, and keep the plant running.
challenges.hint: Three of the unused services have a checkbox on OpenPLC's Settings page. The REST API on 8443 has none: block it with an iptables rule at the top of the PLC container's INPUT chain. Keep Modbus (502) and the web interface (8080) on.

challenges.title: Network Segmentation
challenges.description: Block the attack machine from reaching critical ICS services
challenges.hint: Block the attack machine (172.18.0.100) from accessing the PLC and OPC-UA server

challenges.title: IDS Monitoring & Tuning
challenges.description: Ensure the IDS is running and actively detecting multiple types of attacks
challenges.hint: Start the IDS, ensure it is capturing packets, and trigger at least 3 different detection rules
